issues.description: download_and_untar.sh warns but does not exit when unzip is missing
issues.detail: The script echoes 'unzip is not installed' and continues under set -euo pipefail, then later invokes unzip and dies cryptically. The precondition guard is theater. Either exit non-zero on the check or remove it. A missing precondition must terminate execution.

issues.description: Usage block prints help but does not exit on bad argv
issues.detail: When argc is out of [1,2], the script prints usage and falls through to realpath $1, crashing with an opaque 'unbound variable' error under set -u or silently proceeding with the wrong frame. Add 'exit 1' after the heredoc so precondition violations terminate cleanly.

issues.description: data.sh overwrites utt.list mid-pipeline, destroying its invariant
issues.detail: utt.list is first written from wav filenames, then later overwritten from transcripts.txt after filtering. The two files denote different sets and the second silently shadows the first. Any later reader assuming 'utt.list = utterances with audio' is wrong. Use distinct filenames (utt.wavlist, utt.txtlist).

issues.description: Character-normalization sed chain is opaque with no stated invariant or target alphabet
issues.detail: The pipeline strips a hand-picked set of full-width punctuation and one full-width 'A' via successive sed calls. No comment explains why these characters and not others, no specification of the legal postcondition alphabet, and no tie to the tokenizer. Extract rules into a named mapping or document the target alphabet.

issues.description: README link to ASR config path is wrong
issues.detail: The README references ./conf/train/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml, but the file actually lives at ./conf/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml. A reader following the link gets a 404. Fix the link to match the published artifact.

issues.description: Per-archive extraction blocks are copy-pasted; expected counts are magic numbers
issues.detail: Three TAL_ASR-{1,2,3}.zip blocks repeat the same logic parameterized by archive name and subdir; a loop over a tuple table would be simpler. Likewise, expected utterance counts (22467, 3208, 6072, 29386, 38924) are hard-coded inline rather than named constants with provenance.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a conventional ESPnet recipe addition whose substantive risk lies in two shell scripts. download_and_untar.sh advertises preconditions (unzip present, valid argc) that it does not enforce, allowing downstream stages to proceed with empty data or crash opaquely. data.sh carries an undocumented full-width-character normalization chain and overloads utt.list to mean two different sets within the same script. The README also links to a config path that does not exist. Nothing is fatal to training, but the supporting shell is under-audited and should be tightened before merge.
